function: Channel estimation: LSTM and FC network map pilot sequences to near-field large-scale parameters (AoA, AoD, distance); path gain by LS/LMMSE; full channel reconstructed (pp. 12-17).
system: Downlink THz MIMO-OFDM, BS NT=64 and UE NR=16 planar-array antennas, NRF=4 RF chains, 1 THz band, 120 kHz subcarrier spacing, near-field LoS channel, no RIS (pp. 6, 24-25).
method: LSTM plus FC network (batch norm, leaky-ReLU) trained supervised with MSE loss on the reconstructed channel; meta-learning for new environments is described but not evaluated (pp. 13-18, 23-24).
data_channel: Synthetic near-field LoS THz channels from the paper's own model, Eq. (14): 200K/10K/10K train/validation/test samples; no 3GPP model or measured data in the results (pp. 10, 21, 25).
test_conditions: Same setup for training and testing (UE at 3 km/h within 10 m of BS); NMSE and BER versus SNR and pilot ratio; no unseen scenario (pp. 24-28).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE, CS-based estimation [28]. Learned: CNN-based estimation [29], Transformer-based estimation with similar complexity (pp. 25, 29).
metrics: NMSE and BER (QPSK, hard decision) versus SNR; BER versus pilot-to-channel ratio; training MSE loss; computational complexity in flops (pp. 18-20, 25-28).
complexity: Flops formula 16LNL^2+2NmNF^2+(16LKMT+26L)NL+(5Nm+2NL+8P+5)NF; 3.34e8 flops versus CS 4.96e8-1.30e9 and CNN 1.19e9-6.74e9 (Table I, pp. 18-20).
q1_support: p. 10: "we use the block-fading near-field LoS channel model" (own Eq. 14); p. 25: "The channel samples are generated using (14)". No 3GPP channel model, DeepMIMO, COST 2100, or measured data is stated for training or testing.
q2_support: p. 25: "we generate 200 K, 10 K, and 10 K samples for the training, validation, and testing" from one simulator. Meta-learning for new environments (p. 23: "we exploit the meta-learning") is only described; Figs. 10-13 report SNR and pilot-ratio sweeps, no unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 25: "we use five benchmark schemes": LS, LMMSE, CS-based [28] (non-learned) and "CNN-based channel estimation [29], and 5) Transformer-based channel estimation" (learned); compared on NMSE (Fig. 10, p. 26) and BER (Fig. 11, p. 27).
q4_support: p. 18: "we measure the complexity in terms of the number of floating point operations (flops)"; Table I (p. 20) gives the flops formula and values for D-STiCE.
q5_support: p. 25: "The channel samples are generated using (14)". Synthetic channels from the paper's own model; no code or data link or DOI appears in the paper.
notes: Preprint arXiv:2405.07255v1 (DRAFT); page numbers are file pages, p. 1 is an IEEE submission notice. Area 2: channel estimation. GAN-based data generation and meta-learning (pp. 21-24) are described, but no result in Section V uses them. Ref. [23] is 3GPP TR 38.900, cited only for the simulator (p. 21) without saying the channel follows it, so q1 is 0; reviewer may confirm.
